newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates fall on upcoming payments.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates fall on upcoming payments.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates fell at mid-session on Monday reflecting expectations that upcoming interest payments on government bonds would flush the banking system and loosen market liquidity, dealers said.

The overnight interbank was at 6.005 percent against Saturday's 6.202 close -- still above the central bank's target zone of 5.0-5.5 percent -- with 30-day commercial paper at 5.75-5.85 against 5.85-6.00.
Dealers said they expected the rates to fall further later in the session despite the central bank's scheduled issue of T$5 billion negotiable certificates of deposit.
In the bond market, the 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 5.8400 percent against 5.8200.
